messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: generation-api-prod - sustained GPU queue growth + autoscaler failing to satisfy allocations. Symptoms: queued requests spike, 429 throttles, autoscaler errors referencing 'fragmentation' and 'insufficient_contiguous_vram'. Priority=P1. On-call paged.

ryan_oncall: I'm on call. Pulling metrics and recent deploys. Queue jumped ~00:08 ago.

laura_sre: I see repeated failures in allocator logs: `alloc_slice: failed contiguous: required=4096MB actual_max_contig=3072MB node=node-gpu-09`. Also `autoscaler: at max_replicas=50, desired=58`.

arjun_ml: ML infra here. We recently rolled `mig-profile-2026-03` last week to add 8GB slices for big models and to optimize throughput. Could be interactions with legacy 3GB/4GB set.

ryan_oncall: current cluster summary (quick): total_vram=896GB, free_vram=68GB, usable_slices_by_size: {3GB: 2, 4GB: 5, 8GB: 0}, stranded_vram~50GB (many nodes with <4GB slack). Queue=980, processing=55, throttled=160.

support_maria: we've got an incoming ticket from customer_akela complaining about failures and slow responses for image-generation flow. Notified them "we are investigating".

laura_sre: autoscaler events show `InsufficientContiguousVRAM` and `BinpackReject` for the last 30m. Investigating which nodes are fragmented. Running `ri-debug node-fragmentation --pool gpu-prod --json` now.

ryan_oncall: logs snippet:
```
2865432105Z allocator ERROR node=node-gpu-09 alloc failed required=4096 contiguous=3072
2865432130Z autoscaler WARN scale-request denied reason=InsufficientContiguousVRAM desired=4
2865432161Z queue-manager INFO enqueued=980 processing=59 throttled=152
```

arjun_ml: hypothesis: new 8GB slices removed some 4GB/3GB partitions during drain; remaining VRAM per node isn't aligning with most allocations (many requests ask 4GB). Net effect: fragmented remainder unusable -> stranded_vram.

ops_lead: options for immediate mitigation: A) force rollback of mig-profile to previous (reintroduce 4GB slices), B) run targeted node reprovision to re-image a subset of nodes with clean MIG layout, C) increase autoscaler max and allow oversubscription (risky), D) route some traffic to dedicated/backup pool.

ryan_oncall: quick assessment: increasing max_replicas won't help if allocator can't place slices. Routing to backup pool may help for a subset of customers. I propose: 1) route non-critical tenants (image-gen-beta) to `gpu-spare` pool, 2) start a controlled reprovision of 8 worst-fragmented nodes (one at a time) to coalesce VRAM, 3) prepare rollback of mig-profile if reprovision doesn't help.

deploy-bot: `ROUTE UPDATE generation-api-prod:route(tenant=image-gen-beta)->gpu-spare --user=ryan` -> success.

support_maria: notified impacted customers: image-gen-beta moved to spare pool; commerce-team-prod still on main. We'll send ETA and keep ticket updated.

laura_sre: running reprovision job `./ops/reprovision-node.sh node-gpu-09 --preserve-state=false --mig=clean-4gb-layout` (serial, drain + reprovision).

ryan_oncall: reprovision logs:
```
14:22 cordon node-gpu-09 -> ok
14:24 drain node-gpu-09 -> migrated 10 pods
14:37 reprovision node-gpu-09 -> applied clean MIG layout (4GB/4GB/...) -> reboot
14:45 node-gpu-09 back in pool
14:46 pool usable_slices_by_size: {3GB:2,4GB:8,8GB:2}
14:48 stranded_vram: 28GB
```

laura_sre: after first 2 reprovisions (node-gpu-09 and node-gpu-15), allocator started to place a few more slices. Queue dropped to 420. But still many nodes fragmented.

arjun_ml: note: our workload mix is heavy on 4GB allocations (conversational + image preproc). 8GB-only optimization degraded packing for many real workloads. We should have canaried that profile on a small subset before global rollout.

ops_lead: agreed. For immediate customer protection, continue reprovisioning up to 6 nodes (one at a time) and keep routing non-critical tenants to `gpu-spare`. Also schedule a short maintenance window to run a defragmentation pass across the pool during low traffic.

ryan_oncall: reprovision progress:
```
15:05 node-gpu-15 reprovisioned -> success
15:22 node-gpu-21 reprovision queued -> cordon+drain
15:28 node-gpu-21 reprovisioned -> success
15:40 usable_slices_by_size: {3GB:3,4GB:18,8GB:4}
15:42 stranded_vram: 8GB
15:45 queue=120 processing=210 throttled=18
```

support_maria: customer_akela: "Thanks — traffic seems to be improving, some retries succeeded." we'll keep them posted.

laura_sre: allocator now reports `desired_replicas=54 current=52`, but placement failures are rare. No more `InsufficientContiguousVRAM` errors in the last 12m.

ops_lead: decision log: we're not doing a full global rollback immediately. We're continuing node reprovision to heal fragmentation while scheduling a staged rollback plan if residual fragmentation persists after reprovision of 10 nodes. Post-incident actions: improve canary testing for MIG profile changes, add `stranded_vram` alert at 30GB, add defrag cron job.

ryan_oncall: incident status: mitigated -> running controlled healing. Time to partial mitigation ~00:46. I'll hand off to laura_sre and arjun_ml for postmortem.

support_maria: compiling customer-facing timeline and will send a summary to PMs + ops contacts.

customer_akela: appreciate the quick updates and routing to spare pool.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated->monitoring, severity=P1->P2, duration so far=00:48:42, runbook=fragmentation-heal v1 applied.

laura_sre: opening postmortem ticket PM-6210 and assigning owners: laura_sre, arjun_ml, ops_lead. Draft expected in 72h. Will include timeline, config change that introduced 8GB-only profile, gaps in canary policy, and long-term defragmentation tooling.

ryan_oncall: handing off. All commands and logs uploaded to incident IT-4927. Closing thread for live updates.
